claims.text: The rabbitmq_prometheus plugin serves the broker's metrics in the Prometheus text format on port 15692.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs 'Monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana' (rabbitmq_prometheus, port 15692)

claims.text: By default the plugin's /metrics endpoint returns metrics aggregated across all queues, not one series per queue.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs 'Monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana' (aggregated vs per-object metrics; return_per_object_metrics default false)

claims.text: /metrics/detailed returns only the metric families (named groups of metrics) named in the family parameter; with queue_coarse_metrics, per-queue series with a queue label and the rabbitmq_detailed_ prefix, e.g. rabbitmq_detailed_queue_messages_ready.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs 'Monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana' (/metrics/detailed, family query parameter, queue_coarse_metrics)

claims.text: queue_messages_ready counts messages ready for delivery; queue_messages counts ready plus delivered-unacknowledged. Both gauges. With manual acks (Notifications: autoAck false) RabbitMQ removes a message only once the consumer acknowledges it.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs 'Monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana' metric table; 'Queues'; 'Consumer Acknowledgements'; DonHang.Notifications/OrderEventsConsumer.cs lines 42-55

claims.text: In a Prometheus scrape config, metrics_path replaces the default path /metrics and params adds URL query parameters to each scrape request.
prometheus.yml at stage-3 (lines 13-23) has a job rabbitmq scraping rabbitmq:15692 with metrics_path /metrics/detailed and params family: [queue_coarse_metrics].

The official rabbitmq image used (rabbitmq:4.1.8-management-alpine) has the rabbitmq_prometheus plugin enabled; compose publishes only port 15672 to the host, so 15692 is reached only on the donhang network.
claims.source_hint: Docker Official Image 'rabbitmq' Dockerfile (rabbitmq-plugins enable rabbitmq_prometheus); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml lines 265-282

claims.text: PromQL rate() is meant for counters: it treats any decrease as a counter reset and counts the value after the drop as growth from zero, so its result is never negative and cannot show a gauge going down.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs 'Query functions' (rate: should only be used with counters; breaks in monotonicity treated as counter resets)
